transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’m having a hard time keeping things organized lately. There are just too many moving parts—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions—and I can’t seem to sort out what matters most. I end up working on whatever feels loudest or most urgent in the moment, even when it’s not the thing I should actually be doing.

Do you find that this difficulty with organization and prioritization also happens in other areas of your life, like at home or in personal tasks, or does it seem limited to your work responsibilities?

It’s mostly showing up around work responsibilities, at least that’s where it’s become impossible to ignore. I’ve got all these pieces—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions—and I just can’t keep them sorted anymore. I end up jumping to whatever feels most urgent or loudest, instead of stepping back and figuring out what actually matters first.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of work?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed feeling depressed or losing interest in things in general. It’s more that I’m getting overwhelmed by keeping up with responsibilities.
Have you been feeling more anxious or worried lately, even when there isn't a specific deadline or task pressing on you?
Not really, no. I mean, I get stressed when there’s a lot to juggle, but I haven’t noticed myself feeling anxious or worried for no clear reason when nothing is pressing.
Outside of work, do you find it difficult to stay focused or organized—like with personal projects, household tasks, or even conversations with friends and family?

Yeah… it’s mainly the same pattern I’ve been describing. What pushed me to come in was that I can’t keep all the moving parts organized anymore—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions. I’ll start on whatever feels loudest or most urgent, instead of what actually matters most.
Outside of work, do you have trouble staying focused or organized in your daily life—like managing your schedule, following through on tasks, or keeping track of conversations?

Yes, outside of work it shows up too. I have a hard time organizing the moving parts of regular life, not just job stuff. I’ll start with whatever feels most urgent or noisy in the moment, instead of what actually matters, and then other things fall behind.
Do you often find yourself distracted by unrelated thoughts or have trouble holding information in your mind—for example, following multi-step instructions or remembering what you were just told?

Yes, that happens a lot. If Slack pings, or a browser tab flashes, or even if some visual idea pops into my head, I can completely lose the thread of what I was coding. Then I’ll realize I’ve spent twenty minutes going down some unrelated design rabbit hole instead of staying with what I was doing.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying seated, especially when you need to focus on a task?

Yeah, especially on long design calls. I’ll feel this kind of pressure building up in my body to move, and I end up pacing around my office or switching chairs. I’m still trying to pay attention and look focused, but sitting still gets hard.
Looking back, did you notice similar difficulties with staying focused, being organized, or sitting still when you were a child, like in school or during family activities?

Yes, looking back, it was definitely there in grade school. Teachers would say I was bright, but that I daydreamed a lot. I remember finishing assignments and then forgetting to turn them in, or losing homework folders. That was happening well before I was a teenager.
